**Starts** once #150 is merged, which writes the design.

## Why

#151 makes a whole `read_itinerary` smaller by listing no candidate names, only a count for each stop and stay. Then nothing in the coordinator's context tells it which stop or stay holds a candidate the user names, such as "let's do the Desert Pearl."

A wrong guess fails quietly. `select_user_place` on another stop adds the place there as one the user named, and the stop that offered it stays undecided. `find_place` doesn't help either. It searches Google, not the trip, so a typo such as "Desert Rose" can return a real Desert Rose somewhere else, and never the Desert Pearl Inn.

`find_in_trip` searches the trip's own places by name, with string similarity, and says where each one sits in the trip. It costs tokens only when the user names a place, not on every whole read.

## Design

- [Tool design](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/tools.md), section 2.1: the `find_in_trip` row, and the section "`find_in_trip` finds a place the user names". Section 3: who gets it.
- [Technical spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/technical-spec.md), sections 5.1, 5.2 ("When the user names a place"), and 7.1.

## Open questions

- None.

## Do

- Add `find_in_trip` to `createTripServer()` in `src/tools/trip-server.ts`, with the read-only annotation `read_itinerary` has. The coordinator already gets every tool on the `trip` server (`allowedTools` in `src/agent/coordinator.ts`), so it needs no other change to reach it. No worker gets it (tool design section 3).
- Its one input is the text, a required string, named `text` as in `find_place`'s input (`src/tools/place-input.schema.ts`).
- Load the trip as `read_itinerary` does, with `session.reader.read(session.tripId)` (`src/tools/itinerary-tools.ts`). Search the places the itinerary holds: every stop's and stay's candidates, the rejected places, the start and end places, and the stays' towns. Not the trip's other saved places, which come from searches and were never offered. Each place is listed once, however many spots hold it.
- Match by trigram similarity, written in TypeScript in the tool, with no new package. Lowercase both strings, and take out punctuation and a leading "the", before scoring. Score and break ties as tool design 2.1 says. It always returns the 5 closest, or every place when the trip has fewer. Use `FIND_PLACE_MATCHES` in `src/tools/place-tools.ts` for the 5, since the two tools return the same number. There's no cutoff for a match.
- Write the reply in the format in tool design 2.1. Its first line gives the number returned, such as "The 3 places in the trip closest to "Desert Rose", best first:" on a smaller trip. The lines for each spot, in the order the whole read lists them:
  - `Lodging candidate for Stay 1, Springdale (stay_…), set 1. Selected.` or `Not selected.`
  - `Candidate for Day 12, Stop 5 (stop_…), attraction: "the east end of the South Rim", set 1. Selected.` or `Not selected.`
  - `Rejected for the whole trip: "too far off the route".`
  - `The start place.`, `The end place.`, or, for a loop, `The start and end place.`
  - `The town of Stay 1 (stay_…).`
- The tool's description says it searches only this trip's places, and always returns the closest few, so the coordinator checks that one is the place the user meant. Write the text that names where a place sits, such as `Candidate for Day 12, Stop 5 (stop_…), attraction: "the east end of the South Rim", set 1. Not selected.`, as a function `select_user_place` can use too. #56 gives `select_user_place`'s reply a line in the same form, for each other stop or stay where the place is a candidate. If #56 is merged first and already has such a function, use it here instead of writing a second one.
- Add the rule in technical spec 5.2, "When the user names a place", to the coordinator's instructions (`src/agent/coordinator-prompt.ts`).
- Run `npm run agent-views`, and commit the coordinator's view file with the change.

#151 may be built at the same time. Both change the coordinator's instructions and its view file. Whichever merges second rebases onto `main` and runs `npm run agent-views` again.

## Done when

- Tests show these, on a small trip built in the test with the place names below. The example trips' places are made up, so they don't have these names.
  - "Desert Rose" ranks the Desert Pearl Inn first, ahead of Desert View Watchtower and Rose Well Camp.
  - "Cliffrose" ranks "Cliffrose Springdale, Curio Collection by Hilton" first, ahead of Cliff Palace.
  - Case, punctuation, and a leading "the" don't change the match.
  - A place in two spots, such as a hotel that's also a dinner candidate, gets a line for each.
  - A selected candidate, a rejected place, the start and end place, and a stay's town each get their own line.
  - A place saved by a search but never offered isn't returned.
  - A trip with fewer than 5 places returns all of them, and a trip with none says so, with no error.
- The coordinator's view file shows the new tool and its instructions.
- `npm run check` passes.

## Ends in

A PR.

**Settled in:** the PR.
